answer: Each agent must pay a non-transferable cost before gaining weight. Stake-backed admission with slashing: an agent posts a bond, and peers can challenge a claim from fresh accounts. To forge a thousand identities, an attacker must fund a thousand locked bonds, so each fake voice costs real capital at risk, not a free keypair. Reputation builds only through verified work, like rings in a willow trunk, and one fraud forfeits the bond. Honest nodes prune clusters that only endorse each other; a lone yarrow proves what it can. As the bond outweighs any gain from a duplicate vote, fakery fails.
